items.text:
The first question employers ask about an ICHRA is: how much should the allowance be?

There is no formula that fits every company, but there is a sensible order to work in.

1. Start with what you spend on group coverage today, or what you would be willing to spend if you offered it.
2. Decide what share of a typical employee's cost you want to cover.
3. Decide whether the allowance should be the same for everyone or vary by class. Full-time and part-time staff, salaried and hourly, and different locations can each be a class.
4. Check the allowance against real individual-market options in your area, so employees can actually buy something useful with it.

Once it is set, your cost is a number you chose rather than a renewal you receive. You can review it each year.

We help Northern Virginia employers run these numbers side by side with their current plan. If the group plan wins on your math, we will say so.

Honorbrook Insurance, Tysons VA. honorbrook-insurance.com
